about: Where Google, Amazon (and AWS) and Microsoft stand among the summit's companies, from desks/researcher/centres-of-gravity-evidence-round-1.md (researcher@PrompTugal.dinis, read 6 November 2026, public pages only). Each cell is one relation to one centre with one of three states: found (with its source), searched and not found (with where it was searched), not looked at yet. Absence on page 1 of a list is not absence at the summit. By dev.graphs@PrompTugal.dinis.

partner.text: Google Cloud is listed among Web Summit's 2026 event partners (category AI and machine learning); the newsroom's data has it as a confirmed partner. The partners list shows 40 partners across 8 pages with no tiers, and only page 1 was readable.
partner.label: Google Cloud

speaker.text: No speaker from Google or Google Cloud found in the 2026 speakers page as loaded. Read by researcher@ on 7 November 2026 in a browser, loading the whole page (about 71,000 characters); completeness was not confirmed, so a miss is not proof of absence. Roles only, no names.
speaker.label: Google

builton.label: 3 of 14 read
builton.text: Of the 14 partner companies' pages read, three name Google Cloud: Elastic (on its cloud marketplace), Datadog (a monitoring product page; no partnership claimed) and ManageEngine (cloud security for Azure, AWS and GCP as a product area; coverage, not a partnership). Fourteen of the 17 other companies our data lists as Web Summit partners have now had their front page read (researcher@, batches 1 and 2); three (Akamai, Genspark, PitchBook) refuse a plain fetch and are not read. A page not showing something does not mean the tie is absent. A menu link, a customer story or a rival comparison is not a partnership, and each line says which it is.

builton.label: 11 of 17 sell on AWS Marketplace
builton.text: Two lenses. Front pages (14 of the 17 other partner companies read): five name AWS, in different ways: Cerebras (a testimonial by an AWS vice president on a joint inference setup, not called a partnership), Elastic (on its cloud marketplace), Datadog (a monitoring product page, no partnership claimed), ManageEngine (product coverage) and Runpod (a customer compares AWS as the more expensive rival). AWS Marketplace search by company name (all 17, first results only): 11 have a listing of their own, nine under their own name (1Password, Akamai, Cerebras, Datadog, Elastic, IBM, Runpod, Twilio, VTEX) and two under a parent (Cisco for Cisco Outshift, Zoho for ManageEngine); several hold an AWS Specialization badge. A listing shows the company sells there; it is not a stated partnership. A front page understates the tie (Twilio and VTEX said nothing on theirs yet both sell there), so the marketplace is the better first source. Not found in the first results: Mozilla, Gcore, Genspark, KPMG and PitchBook, and the search is fuzzy, so that is not proof of none. Delinea appears only through resellers. The Google Cloud and Microsoft marketplaces are not read yet.
